name: Shah-Fazil
near: Safed-Bulan (Safedbulan; called Gulistan in some sources), the complex is in the village itself: 2GIS — 42a Muzeynaya St. (or 40/1 A. Shaitov St.). Kerben — ~10 km (Destination Jalal-Abad); Ala-Buka — 15 km per open.kg, ~50 km per Destination Jalal-Abad (discrepancy). It is ~5 km to the border with Uzbekistan (too.kg).
elev: Not confirmed: the elevation of Safed-Bulan village is not given in the sources found (roughly the foothills of the Chatkal Range; check on a map).
short: Shah-Fazil is a Karakhanid-era mausoleum (11th–12th centuries) with a unique truncated-pyramid dome and carved ganch plaster in the village of Safed-Bulan; the centre of a revered pilgrimage complex with the sacred Archa-Mazar mountain and the women-only Safed-Bulan mausoleum.
desc: The Shah-Fazil mausoleum is one of the rare monuments of the Karakhanid era: a building square in plan with a dome in the form of a truncated pyramid, its walls inside covered with carved ganch (gypsum plaster) ornament (too.kg, Destination Jalal-Abad). The dating in the sources is the 11th or 11th–12th centuries (too.kg, 24.kg); mir24 gives the 9th century. According to legend, about 2,700 warriors spreading Islam, led by Shah-Jarir, died here during Friday prayers; his widow turned grey with grief — hence the name Safed-Bulan (“white Bulan”); his son Shah-Fazil later peacefully completed the Islamization of the north of Fergana and is buried in the mausoleum (too.kg). The complex includes the sacred mountain Archa-Mazar, the mausoleums of Alambardar and Safed-Bulan (19th century, women only), a mosque of the 17th–19th centuries, a hermit's cave and a pre-Islamic upright stone — the “fertility stone” (too.kg, Destination Jalal-Abad, 24.kg). The monument has been state-protected since 2002 and is on UNESCO's Tentative List (Silk Roads Sites in Kyrgyzstan); in 2025 it was visited by more than 33,000 people; a new 400 m² museum building is being built by the end of 2026 (mir24).
guide: Shah-Fazil is surprising for its shape: there is no other pyramid-shaped dome like it in Central Asia, and inside the walls are covered with the finest ganch carving almost a thousand years old. It is an active pilgrimage site: people come here from Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan, so dress modestly and keep quiet. Women should visit the Safed-Bulan mausoleum — entry there is for women only, and in the courtyard there is a “fertility stone” where people pray for children. Climb the sacred Archa-Mazar mountain — from it you can see the whole complex and the valley by the Uzbek border. The complex is open daily from 8:00 to 17:00, so come in the morning — the road from Jalal-Abad is not short.
see: The Shah-Fazil mausoleum (pyramid dome, carved ganch); the sacred Archa-Mazar mountain; the mausoleums of Alambardar (the standard-bearer) and Safed-Bulan (women only); a mosque of the 17th–19th centuries; the hermit's cave; the pre-Islamic “fertility stone”; a Bronze Age monument (24.kg); the reserve museum (new building — by the end of 2026, mir24).
skip: You aren't interested in Islamic architecture and pilgrimage sites. You don't have a whole day: the road from Jalal-Abad is long and accommodation is far. You're coming only for nature — this is first and foremost a shrine.
diff: Easy: a tour of the complex in the village; the climb up Archa-Mazar mountain is short, easy to medium (editorial).
when: April–October (warm season, convenient road — editorial); the complex operates year-round. On religious holidays there are many pilgrims (editorial).
daytime: Morning — fewer people and soft light for photographing the dome; arrive at the 8:00 opening so you can get back to Jalal-Abad before dark (editorial).
how: From Jalal-Abad: shared taxi to Kerben (~400 som), then a taxi to Safed-Bulan/Gulistan (~1,000 som) and on foot to the mausoleum; a private car from Jalal-Abad — ~5,000 som one way (Destination Jalal-Abad). Kerben is ~10 km from the complex. From Bishkek — about 600 km (mir24).
needcar: Yes: you need a car/taxi to reach the village; around the complex — on foot.
self: Yes: the complex is open to visitors, no permits needed. Observe the shrine's rules; the Safed-Bulan mausoleum is for women only (too.kg, 24.kg).
roadtype: Paved road to Kerben/Ala-Buka, then village roads to Safed-Bulan (editorial, not confirmed by a source).
traveltime: Not confirmed: the exact time from Jalal-Abad is not given in the sources; roughly 3–4 h by car (editorial, estimated from the distance via Tash-Kumyr and Kerben).
stay: The nearest accommodation is in Ala-Buka (Destination Jalal-Abad, “about 50 km”); too.kg mentions cafés, shops and accommodation in Gulistan/Safed-Bulan. Names and prices not found; TripAdvisor shows nearby hotels without verified prices.
net: There is mobile coverage (too.kg). Operators not specified.
entry: Not confirmed: the amount of an entrance fee/donation was not found in the sources; the complex has the status of a museum-reserve (2GIS) — a museum fee is possible, check on site.
transfer: Jalal-Abad — Kerben shared taxi ~400 som; Kerben — Safed-Bulan taxi ~1,000 som; a private car from Jalal-Abad ~5,000 som one way (Destination Jalal-Abad, year not given).
bring: Modest clothing (long sleeves and a skirt/trousers; a headscarf for women; editorial for Muslim shrines); cash in som for taxis, donations and souvenirs (souvenirs are sold at the entrance — 24.kg); water and a hat for the climb up Archa-Mazar.
warn: An active pilgrimage site: keep quiet and follow the dress code; the Safed-Bulan mausoleum is for women only. The complex is ~5 km from the border with Uzbekistan (too.kg) — do not approach the border. Shah-Fazil is only on UNESCO's Tentative List (Silk Roads Sites in Kyrgyzstan); the claims of some websites (open.kg, 24.kg) about inclusion in the World Heritage List in 1999 are not confirmed.
food: Not confirmed: cafés in Safed-Bulan are mentioned by too.kg without names; in Kerben and Ala-Buka — southern Kyrgyz cuisine (plov, samsa — editorial).
reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 85 ratings (03.10.2026). 2GIS — rating not displayed. According to mir24: more than 33,000 visitors a year (+10%), including pilgrims from Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan. Typical impressions: unique architecture, an atmosphere of calm; a downside is the remoteness and little infrastructure.
p.sum: The Shah-Fazil complex stands in the village of Safed-Bulan (Gulistan) ~10 km from Kerben, by the border with Uzbekistan. From Jalal-Abad — a shared taxi to Kerben (~400 som) and a taxi to the complex (~1,000 som per car) or a private car (~5,000 som one way); from Bishkek — a subsidized Asman Airlines flight to Kerben (3,600 som, twice a week, 01.2026). Open daily 08:00–17:00; dress modestly, the Safed-Bulan mausoleum is for women only. It makes sense to combine with Sary-Chelek (Arkyt) and Chatkal (via Ala-Buka).

p.season: April–May and September–October — comfortable weather. Summer — hot (Fergana Valley), go in the morning. Winter — accessible, mild. The peak of pilgrims is at religious holidays.
p.budget.economy: Shared taxi Jalal-Abad — Kerben ~400 som ×2 + taxi 1,000 som/car + food ~300 som ≈ 1,500–2,100 som/person per day
p.budget.comfort: A private car from Jalal-Abad ~5,000 som one way (~10,000 round trip) or a Bishkek — Kerben flight 3,600 som + taxi
p.permits: No border-zone permit required (not on the list of border zones), but the area is ~5 km from the Uzbek border — keep your passport with you. Entrance fee/donation not found (museum-reserve status — a fee is possible, check on site). Hours: daily 08:00–17:00 (2GIS, 2026).
p.access: With kids and older people — yes, the complex is in the village, with short distances; the climb up Archa-Mazar mountain is a trail. Wheelchair — partly (uneven grounds). Dogs — no (a holy place).
